new_statements.quote: Usamos de dous accentos, hum agudo, & outro circumflexo. O agudo serve para carregar sobre a vogal, v. g. Sambé, paga. Ordinariamente se acha na derradeira vogal de todos os vocabulos desta lingua, excepto algũas palavras que náo acabaõ em agudo, como Bæ, De, & alguns poucos vocabulos, que a experiencia ensinará. Sobre o til não se poem accento agudo, para evitar a confusaõ na escritura; mas basta advertir que o til sempre he agudo. ... E havendo outros accentos agudos na mesma dicção, he sinal q̃ he composta, & cada huma das partes fica na composiçam com o seu accento agudo: v.g. Tçohóhehéde, estaõ alguns poucos.
new_statements.translation: We use two accents, an acute and a circumflex. The acute serves to bear down on [stress] the vowel, e.g. Sambé 'pay'. Ordinarily it is found on the last vowel of all the words of this language, except some words that do not end in an acute, such as Bæ, De, and a few other words which experience will teach. No acute is written over the tilde, to avoid confusion in writing; but it suffices to note that the tilde [vowel] is always acute [stressed]. ... And when there are further acute accents in the same word, it is a sign that it is a compound, and each of the parts stays in the compound with its own acute accent: e.g. Tçohóhehéde 'there are a few'.
new_statements.citation: Mamiani, Luis Vincencio. 1699. Arte de grammatica da lingua brasilica da naçam Kiriri. Lisboa: Miguel Deslandes. [2a ed. Rio de Janeiro: Bibliotheca Nacional, 1877, same passage p. 4]
new_statements.locator: Parte I, §I 'Da orthographia, & pronunciação', 1699 ed. p. 5 (archive.org artedegrammatica00mami leaf n24); = 1877 ed. p. 4 (p. 93 of artedegrammatic02rovegoog; render saved)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened (archive.org artedegrammatica00mami leaf n24 = printed p. 5, header 'Da Naçaõ Kiriri. 5') and the 1877 render printed p. 4). The passage is there verbatim: 'Usamos de dous accentos, hum agudo, & outro circumflexo. O agudo serve para carregar sobre a vogal, v. g. Sambé, paga. Ordinariamente se acha na derradeira vogal de todos os vocabulos desta lingua, excepto algũas palavras que náo acabaó em agudo, como Bæ, De, & alguns poucos vocabulos, que a experiencia ensinará. Sobre o til não se poem accento agudo.. mas basta advertir que o til sempre he agudo. [elided sentence: Quando o vocabulo acaba em A, ou Æ sem accento, & sem til, se pronuncîa essa vogal a meya boca mal pronunciad…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (marked by the acute) falls on the final vowel of the word as the ordinary rule; a small set of words (Bæ, De and 'a few others') are lexical exceptions; nasal (tilde) vowels are always stressed; in compounds each member keeps its own stress, so a word with two acutes is a compound.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described as such; compounds retain one stress per member (multiple acutes = compound).
new_statements.exceptions: 'algũas palavras que náo acabaõ em agudo, como Bæ, De, & alguns poucos vocabulos, que a experiencia ensinará'; final unaccented A/Æ (no acute, no tilde) is pronounced reduced 'como E Francez no fim da palavra' (e.g. Pide 'está', Tekiébæ 'não veyo').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level orthoepic rule from a 1699 missionary ear-witness grammar of KIPEÁ Kiriri (Bahia), stated over citation/orthographic forms; not a description of the Alagoas Kariri-Xocó community's lost language. Queiroz 2008 p. 89 concurs second-hand ('Kipeá predominantemente oxítono').
new_statements.identity_note: kari1255 'Karirí-Xocó' (ISO kzw) is an ethnonym-based entry with no linguistic corpus of its own: the Porto Real do Colégio (AL) community had shifted to Portuguese before any description (Trujillo Ferrari 1956; Kroeker 1961 in Meader 1978 got 24 remembered words, partly Fulniô, filed under 'Xukurú-Karirí'). Glottolog 5.3 lists it as Unclassifiable with only Kipeá/Kariri-family refs attached, and the Glottolog GitHub master has already moved it to book1242 Bookkeeping. The statement quoted (Mamiani 1699 p. 5 = 1877 p. 4) describes KIPEÁ Kiriri = Glottolog kipe1235, a dialect under Kariri kari1254, which is ALREADY in the catalog (keyed kari1254, named 'Dzubukuá', source Queiroz 2012, reading lexical). The community's revived 'Kariri-Xocó (Dzubukuá Kipeá)' language (Kariri-Xocó et al. 2020) is likewise Kariri kari1254. Recommendation: do not create a kari1255 catalog entity (would double-count Kariri); if the Mamiani final-stress statement is wanted, key it to kipe1235 (Kipeá) as a dialect-level record alongside the Dzubukuá (dzub1241) record, as the kari1254 check note already proposed.

sources.note: §I 'Da orthographia, & pronunciação', p. 5: the acute accent marks stress and 'Ordinariamente se acha na derradeira vogal de todos os vocabulos desta lingua', except a few words (Bæ, De and 'alguns poucos vocabulos'); final unaccented A/Æ is reduced like French final e; a word with more than one acute is a compound, each member keeping its own stress. Describes KIPEÁ Kiriri (kipe1235), not the Alagoas Kariri-Xocó.
